title: Microsoft Teams: new SlimCore-based VDI optimisation for Omnissa Horizon on Mac endpoints
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly says there is no new data store and that the optimisation acts only during calls or meetings. Microsoft documents local logs and other endpoint data, and initialisation when Teams starts; the networking description also needs to retain the virtual-machine screen-sharing exception.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Scope: Users; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Microsoft plans new SlimCore-based Teams VDI optimisation for Omnissa on Mac endpoints, with expanded features and quality, reliability and performance improvements.
claims.quote: This feature allows Mac endpoints to optimize Microsoft Teams in VDI environments with the new SlimCore-based media engine, providing an expanded feature set and multiple improvements in quality, reliability and performance.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The new architecture runs the SlimCore media engine on the user's endpoint rather than running that engine in the virtual desktop.
claims.quote: SlimCore media engine (on the client) and msteams.exe (on the virtual desktop) now have a bidirectional channel and can start processing multimedia requests.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Learn currently documents Windows endpoints for AVD/W365, Citrix, Omnissa and Amazon, but Mac only for AVD/W365 and Citrix.
claims.quote: The new optimization supports Windows endpoints for AVD/W365, Citrix, Omnissa and Amazon. Mac is only supported on AVD/W365 and Citrix.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: MsTeamsPluginOmnissa.dll is bundled with Horizon Client for Windows 8.17 (2512) or higher.
claims.quote: For Omnissa Horizon, MsTeamsPluginOmnissa.dll is bundled with the Horizon Client for Windows 8.17 (2512) or higher.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe the new Omnissa-on-Mac combination; the briefing uses the roadmap and general SlimCore documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: Omnissa Horizon Mac SlimCore new Teams optimization minimum client plugin installation default. Opened vdi-2 and teams-client-vdi-requirements-deploy; Mac coverage is AVD/W365 and Citrix, and Omnissa's new client requirements specify Windows.

claims.where: Why it matters: first sentence; rationale: risk
claims.claim: This change moves existing Horizon Mac call media processing from the virtual desktop to the Mac.
claims.quote: Searched: Omnissa Teams WebRTC optimization Mac endpoint media processing local device existing optimization; Omnissa media endpoint WebRTC optimization architecture. Read vdi-2 and teams-client-vdi-requirements-deploy; neither establishes this prior Horizon Mac processing location.
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence of Why it matters with 'This introduces the SlimCore media engine for Teams users connecting to Horizon desktops from Macs.' In the risk rationale replace 'Call media moves from the virtual desktop to a new media engine process on the Mac' with 'The planned optimisation uses a new SlimCore media engine on the Mac'. Do not claim where the previous optimisation processed calls.

claims.where: Why it matters: architecture paragraph
claims.claim: The endpoint media engine carries out all the network activity for the new architecture.
claims.quote: For Omnissa, Amazon or for MAC (Citrix or AVD/W365), the sharing is done directly between the user's virtual machine -the presenter- and the other peer -viewer- or conference server
claims.fix: Replace the second sentence of Why it matters with 'Learn describes SlimCore media and signalling connections from the endpoint to peers or Teams servers; for Omnissa, outgoing screen sharing is sent from the virtual machine.' This retains the source's screen-sharing exception and avoids assigning its Windows executable name to an undocumented Horizon Mac implementation. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/vdi-2.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: In the documented SlimCore architecture, call media flows directly as SRTP between the endpoint media engine and peers or Teams servers.
claims.quote: Then, Secure Real-time Transport Protocol (SRTP) media flows directly between MsTeamsVdi.exe and the other peer (or Teams Transport Relays or Conference servers).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: There is no new data store.
claims.quote: Logs are stored in the following directory on the user's device: ~/Library/Application Support/Microsoft/TeamsVDI
claims.fix: Remove 'No new data store: the change is about where audio, video and screen-sharing media is processed.' Retain the following SRTP sentence. Learn documents endpoint logs for supported Mac deployments, so an unqualified absence of a new data store is not justified.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: The new Mac optimisation uses a media engine package downloaded and installed on the Mac.
claims.quote: Therefore, the SlimCore package that is fetched and installed on macOS is the Framework only ('Microsoft.Teams.SlimCoreVdiBndl.mac').

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: For the documented AVD/W365 and Citrix Mac deployments, the plugin installs the media engine automatically and silently.
claims.quote: Mac is now rolled out 100% to General Availability for AVD/W365 and Citrix environments. The Plugin is in charge of virtual channel establishment and automatic and silent media engine installation on the Mac device.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions: plugin delivery
claims.claim: Horizon Client for Mac plugin and media engine delivery is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Omnissa Horizon Mac SlimCore new Teams optimization minimum client plugin installation default. Opened vdi-2 and teams-client-vdi-requirements-deploy; the Mac installation section covers AVD/W365 and Citrix, and Omnissa plugin bundling specifies Windows.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The feature acts only when a user makes or joins a call or meeting.
claims.quote: Once you meet all the minimum requirements, launching Teams for the first time will attempt to load in SlimCore optimized mode, by default.
claims.fix: Replace this bullet with 'The documented optimisation is initialised when Teams starts; call media is processed when users make or join calls or meetings.' Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/vdi-2.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Omnissa outgoing screen sharing is sent from the virtual machine, whose network must allow Microsoft 365 endpoint IDs 11 and 12.
claims.quote: For Omnissa, Amazon or for MAC (Citrix or AVD/W365), the sharing is done directly between the user's virtual machine ... therefore administrators must allow ID 11 and 12 on the VM's network

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: VDI2Optimization controls eligibility for SlimCore optimisation, and the VDI partner's policy engines do not control this mode.
claims.quote: This policy now has an additional argument as the only configuration point to control whether or not a user can get the new optimization mode based on SlimCore. In other words, the VDI Partner's policy engines don't control the new optimization mode
